title: Calibration-aware dispatch for hybrid quant kernels
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Scope: implement a runtime dispatch layer that uses packaged quantization profiles (FP8/INT8) plus an automated calibration handoff to select the optimal kernel path per-model and per-batch. Goal is to enable safe mixed-precision execution (FP16/FP8/INT8) while guaranteeing accuracy regressions are within configured thresholds and providing deterministic fallbacks for high-risk inputs. This ticket covers: (1) profile artifact format & integrity checks, (2) runtime micro-validation handshake, (3) dispatch policy with confidence thresholds and telemetry gating, (4) packaging calibration results (calpack) for shipping between offline calibration and runtime, and (5) accuracy validation hooks and alerting when drift is detected.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime accepts and validates a 'calpack' artifact containing per-layer scale tables, per-op accuracy deltas, and a fingerprint. Corrupt or version-mismatched artifacts are rejected with clear error codes.
Dispatch decision created per-request that chooses FP16/FP8/INT8 kernel using the calpack metadata + live micro-validation; decision is logged to telemetry and traceable in Console.

If micro-validation on a sampled mini-batch exceeds configured KL/perplexity thresholds, runtime aborts quantized path and falls back to FP16 for that request; fallbacks incur a trace event and metric increment.

Automated end-to-end eval: baseline vs quantized model on the canonical validation set shows <1.5% change in generation-divergence and <2% change in task accuracy for selected INT8 profiles (numbers surfaced in release notes).
E2E tests and unit tests covering artifact parsing, handshake failure modes, fallback logic, and telemetry emission are added and passing on CI.
design_decisions: Use a compact 'calpack' artifact (protobuf v2 compat) with versioned schema: model_hash, per-layer dtype candidate list, scales, expected delta metrics, and validation seed set ids.

Perform a two-step runtime handshake: (A) quick signature + metadata integrity check, (B) optional sampled micro-validation (configurable sample size) executing a fixed set of short prompts to verify distributional assumptions before switching to a quantized kernel.

Policy semantics: prefer lower-cost quantized kernel only if both artifact-reported safety flag==OK and micro-validation delta < runtime-configured threshold. Otherwise fallback to FP16. Drift events will trigger gradual rollback and a rerun of offline calibration pipeline.

Telemetry: emit per-decision fields (chosen_path, artifact_version, microval_kl, microval_ppl, fallback_reason) so Console can surface regressions and allow rule-based rollouts (canary -> 50% -> 100%).
implementation_notes: Add CalpackVerifier component in runtime that performs schema validation and signature verification against customer-managed keys (if provided).
Micro-validation harness reuses eval harness from research with deterministic RNG seeds; limit to 8 short prompts for a quick check (configurable).
Dispatch table maps (model_hash, token_length_bucket, customer_tier) -> preferred quant candidates with hard thresholds to avoid flapping.
Introduce a lightweight sampling controller that tags 1% of requests for 'shadow-quant' runs to collect real production divergence metrics before any rollout increase.
Edge-case: models with adaptive softmax heads require special handling (skip INT8 for final softmax and recompute in FP16). Add a flag in calpack to mark ops excluded from quantization.
test_plan: Unit: parsing, signature, and version mismatch tests for calpack.
Integration: runtime handshake + micro-validation passes/fails with synthetic tensors to exercise KL thresholds.
Perf: throughput comparison FP16 vs INT8 vs FP8 on representative sequence lengths; ensure batching latency SLOs maintained.
Regression: end-to-end generation comparison on the canonical regression set (200 prompts) with numeric thresholds asserted in CI.
Chaos: force corrupted calpack and simulate transient failures to validate safe fallback and metrics emission.
